summary: Thomas Watters was a scholar in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Queen's University Belfast in 1857 and earned a B.A. from Queen's University of Ireland around 1857–1861.

Thomas William Rhys Davids worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics, earning his Ph.D. at the University of Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler. He founded the Pali Text Society and held posts at UCL, Manchester, and the Royal Asiatic Society.
Thomas Zehnder is an Indologist and linguist. He completed his PhD at the University of Zurich, studying under supervisor Alexander Lubotsky.

Thomé H. Fang worked in philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at National Central University from around 1929 to 1948 and at National Taiwan University from approximately 1948 to 1973.

Thubten Yeshe was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Sera Monastery under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and Trijang Rinpoche. He co-founded Kopan Monastery, founded FPMT, and held visiting posts at Middlebury College and the University of Virginia.

Thubten Zopa Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied under Thubten Yeshe, Trijang Rinpoche, and Denma Lochö Rinpoche. He co-founded Kopan Monastery by 1971 and founded the Lama Yeshe Wisdom Archive in 1996.

Thupten Jinpa studied at Ganden Shartse Monastery and the University of Cambridge. Active in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he taught at Ganden Shartse, was a research fellow at Girton College, and became chief editor at the Institute of Tibetan Classics.

Théodore Pavie was an Indologist and Sinologist who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held the Sanskrit chair at the Collège de France from 1852 to 1857 and later served at the Catholic University of the West from around 1875 to 1885.

Thích Minh Châu was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University around 1957–1964 and served as a lecturer in Chinese at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, attested in 1984.

Thích Thiện Châu was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He pursued his higher education in France, studying at Paris-Sorbonne University around 1967–1971 and Sorbonne Nouvelle University around 1971–1977.

Tianshu Zhu specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, earning an MA from Northwest University and a PhD from Ohio State under John C. Huntington. Zhu held posts at Northwest University, Shaanxi History Museum, Ohio State, and Korea University.

Tilak Kariyawasam is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as head of Pali and Buddhist Studies at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1993) and as Dean of the Graduate School at International Buddhist College (attested 2014).

Tilmann Vetter worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, earning his PhD from the University of Vienna under Erich Frauwallner. He was a professor at Leiden University, serving there from 1974 and holding a professorship around 1976–2002.

Tim Dean studied at the University of East Anglia, Brandeis University, and Johns Hopkins University. He held academic posts at the University of Washington (circa 1993–1998), University at Buffalo (circa 2002–2018), and University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (circa 2018).

Timothy H. Barrett is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied at Cambridge and Yale. He taught at the University of Cambridge (attested 1981) and became a professor at SOAS University of London in 1986.

Timothy Lenz is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed graduate studies at the University of Washington under Richard Salomon and Collett Cox. He held positions at the University of Washington, where he was attested as professor in 2017.
Timothy Lubin is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his PhD from Columbia University by 1994. He held an academic post at Washington and Lee University, attested in 2020.
Tina Rasmussen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied under traditional teacher Pa-Auk Sayadaw and completed her master's degree under supervisor Christian K. Wedemeyer.

Tissa Rajapatirana is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong between 1966 and 1974. He held a post at the Australian National University, attested in 1988.
Tiziana Pontillo is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. She studied at the University of Cagliari in 2016 and held a post there in 2022.
